title: Atlas amendments reach a vote only when a Ranked Delegate stakes their own capital behind them
content:
A.1.11.2.1.3 gates the entire Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle behind a bonded sponsor: a proposal "can proceed to a vote only if it is triggered by a Ranked Delegate whose AD Buffer contains at least the Triggering Threshold... at the time of triggering," verified by the Core Facilitator. A.1.12.2.1.2 imposes the same requirement in the Monthly Cycle. Authorship is unrestricted; *triggering* is not, and "A Ranked Delegate may trigger a Proposal they authored" only if they meet the threshold themselves.

The Action Tenet at A.1.11.2.1.3.0.4.2 names the purpose: "To deter spurious or misaligned proposals, Ranked Delegates must 'stake' a portion of their AD Buffer to trigger a Proposal." The stake "remains in effect until the triggered Proposal is fully resolved" — either rejection by the Core Facilitator for misalignment, or the conclusion of a Sky Governance vote — and is forfeited on either failure path.

The lock is enforced against the delegate's own income. The scenario at A.1.11.2.1.3.0.4.2.1.1 finds it *aligned* for the Core Facilitator to withhold a triggering delegate's compensation while other delegates are paid, because "paying out the AD Buffer would have led to Entity's AD Buffer dropping below the required Triggering Threshold while the Proposal was still unresolved." Sponsorship therefore has a real carrying cost, not just a contingent one.

What this design prices is not the proposal but the *attention*. Voter attention is the scarce resource in any amendable constitution, and Sky rations it by requiring someone with standing and capital to answer for each demand on it. A tie-break follows for the same reason: where several delegates signal intent, "the first Ranked Delegate to post a reply... shall be treated as the triggering Ranked Delegate," so exactly one party is on the hook.
description: Triggering requires the Triggering Threshold in the delegate's AD Buffer, which is locked until resolution and forfeited if the proposal is voted down — pricing the right to consume voter attention.
